facts.statement: Aegyptosuchus fossils were discovered in the Bahariya Formation of Egypt from the Cenomanian age of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: It was found in the Bahariya Formation of Egypt, which dates back to the Cenomanian age of the Late Cretaceous.

facts.statement: Only one species, Aegyptosuchus peyeri, has been described for this genus found in the Bahariya Formation of Egypt.
facts.quote: Sólo se ha descrito una especie, Aegyptosuchus peyeri, encontrada en la Formación Bahariya de Egipto

facts.statement: The holotype specimen SPG 1912 VIII 177 is a thick-skulled cranium characterized by small dorsotemporal fossae.
facts.quote: el espécimen holotipo SPG 1912 VIII 177, un techo craneal caracterizado por el grosor del mismo y las pequeñas fosas dorsotemporales

facts.statement: Additional fossil remains including teeth and various vertebrae were lost during World War II bombings of Munich.
facts.quote: además de restos adicionales consistentes en dientes y vértebras caudales, cervicales, sacrales y presacrales, los cuales infortunadamente se perdieron por los bombardeos sobre la ciudad de Múnich en la Segunda Guerra Mundial.

facts.statement: The genus Aegyptosuchus was named by Stromer in 1933.
Aegyptosuchus belongs to the family Aegyptosuchidae, which also includes the genus Aegisuchus.
facts.quote: Aegyptosuchus is a member of the family Aegyptosuchidae, along with the genus Aegisuchus.

facts.statement: The family Aegyptosuchidae is part of the clade Eusuchia and is considered the sister group to the crown group Crocodylia.
facts.quote: Aegyptosuchidae belongs to the clade Eusuchia, and is proposed to be the sister clade to the crown group Crocodylia, which contains all extant (living) crocodilians.

facts.statement: Carroll classified the genus Aegyptosuchus into the family Stomatosuchidae in 1988.
facts.quote: Carroll (1988) clasificó posteriormente a este género en la familia Stomatosuchidae.

facts.statement: Holliday and Gardner reclassified Aegyptosuchus into the family Aegyptosuchidae in 2012, viewing it as distinct from stomatosuchids and closely related to Aegisuchus.
facts.quote: Holliday & Gardner (2012) consideraron a Aegyptosuchus como distinto de los estomatosúquidos y lo volvieron a incluir en la familia Aegyptosuchidae, como pariente cercano de Aegisuchus.

facts.statement: Aegyptosuchus lived during the Cenomanian stage, between 100.5 and 93.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Cenomanian to Cenomanian (100.5 to 93.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: Aegyptosuchus is notable for its thick cranial roof.
facts.quote: un techo craneal caracterizado por el grosor del mismo
